style.vernacular: Low city of timber houses clad in corrugated iron painted red, blue, yellow, green and white with contrasting roofs and window frames; cheap reinforced-concrete houses and apartment blocks from the early 20th century on, often painted or finished with a dashed mineral/shell render in white, cream or grey; functionalist and modernist concrete public buildings with flat or low roofs; steel-and-glass towers and halls (Harpa) and big-box malls on the edges. Few trees (birch, spruce), lava fields and treeless coast around.
style.ornament: Corrugated iron cladding in bright paint, white window frames, steep gabled roofs on old houses and low flat roofs on modernist ones, gable-fronted concrete houses of the Guðjón Samúelsson school, basalt-column motifs in civic buildings, lava rock and moss as landscaping.

sources.what: corrugated iron cladding as a distinctly Icelandic feature, bright painted wooden houses, early concrete houses, steep pitched and low modernist roofs, functionalism from the 1930s with mineral and seashell dashed finishes, turf houses
